claims.text: LPBF of mixed refractory-element and Cu powders can enable large-scale synthesis of composite structures.
LPBF can produce a stable, refined microstructure in a refractory-alloy/Cu composite.
The feedstock is a blend of initially unalloyed or weakly bonded refractory-alloy elements and Cu.
LPBF can promote in-situ alloy formation from the refractory-element/Cu powder blend.
High-energy laser exposure rapidly melts and resolidifies the refractory-element/Cu mixture.
LPBF produces high cooling rates and minimal diffusion during the build.
LPBF melting and solidification establish a refined dendritic or cellular microstructure.
The refined microstructure kinetically traps Cu within the refractory matrix.
Kinetic trapping minimizes phase segregation of Cu.
Positive heat of mixing between Cu and refractory alloying elements creates a thermodynamic tendency toward phase segregation.
The extremely high heating and cooling rates of LPBF overcome this thermodynamic segregation tendency.
LPBF produces a metastable composite microstructure in which Cu is uniformly integrated with the refractory matrix.
The resulting composite will have a uniformly mixed microstructure with reduced Cu segregation.
The resulting composite will be more suitable for nuclear-reactor cooling applications.
Conventional alloying methods such as arc melting cause extensive refractory-element/Cu phase separation because they cool slowly and permit ample diffusion.
Successful in-situ alloy formation requires sufficient laser energy density and optimized LPBF parameters.
Insufficient laser energy can cause incomplete alloying.
Excessive laser energy can cause evaporation or defects.
The precise LPBF process window and long-term stability under reactor conditions remain experimentally unvalidated.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome describe the microstructure as stable, while the mechanism calls it metastable and the uncertainty field states that long-term stability has not been validated. Kinetic stability could reconcile these statements, but that distinction is not explicitly made.
